resources.string: Set up BioKey
Lock any app behind %1$s
Its storage was cleared some time after %1$s, when BioKey last ran, and every lock and record went with it. Once setup is done, this is recorded in Security activity.
Its storage was cleared at an unknown time (the phone’s clock was changed), and every lock and record went with it. Once setup is done, this is recorded in Security activity.
What waits a day

For a day after setup is done, you can’t mark Security activity as reviewed or clear it, switch off “Failed unlock alerts”, “Also record screen lock unlocks” or “Diagnostic log”, or delete the diagnostic log. Anything else you change meanwhile is recorded in Security activity.
Allow restricted settings
Android blocks the switch for apps installed from a file. Try it once, then tap here: in BioKey’s App info, open the ⋮ menu at the top and choose “Allow restricted settings”.
If Android wouldn’t let you turn it on
Tap here: in BioKey’s App info, open the ⋮ menu at the top and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then turn BioKey on.
Allow usage access
Advanced Protection is on, so BioKey uses compatibility mode: this tells it which app was opened and whether a locked app is still on screen
Allow display over other apps
Lets BioKey cover a locked app as it opens
Turn on BioKey in Accessibility settings
Lets BioKey see which app is on screen, so it can cover locked ones
Lets BioKey see which app is on screen, so it can cover locked ones. In the list that opens, tap %1$s under “Downloaded apps” and turn it on.
Not on yet. Tap here and turn on the switch at the top of the page.

When you finish, BioKey also locks the apps it recognises, such as banking, chat, email, camera, photos and web browsers, and sorts them into its Personal, Finance, Social and Work profiles. Change them on BioKey’s main page. Turning off “%1$s” in BioKey’s settings stops it locking apps you install later. Apps it has already locked stay locked.
